Looking at the requirements, I need to create a topology figure showing a branch office WAN network with:
- 2 access switches
- 1 branch router  
- 2 regional hub routers
- 4 links connecting them as specified

Since this is a network topology, I'll use the `topology` genre (experimental, so requires the experimental/topology.md reference). Here's the FigDown document:

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 topology
title "Branch office WAN uplinks"

node access1 "Access Switch 1"
node access2 "Access Switch 2"
node branch "Branch Router"
node hubprimary "Regional Hub (Primary)"
node hubbackup "Regional Hub (Backup)"

edge access1 branch
edge access2 branch
edge branch hubprimary "Primary WAN"
edge branch hubbackup "Backup WAN"
```

This document defines:
- **Five nodes** with the requested IDs and descriptive labels
- **Four edges** representing the links: 
  - Both access switches connecting to the branch router (local switching)
  - Branch router to primary hub (primary WAN uplink)
  - Branch router to backup hub (backup WAN uplink for diversity/redundancy)

The labels on the WAN links make the primary/backup distinction clear. When rendered, this will show a typical branch office architecture with dual regional connectivity for high availability.
